title: Grateful Dead Live at Poplar Creek Music Theater on 1983-06-27
source: Sennheisser 421s>Sony TCD5M>cassette>Sony TCD5M; FOB Recorded by the late George "Fingers" Bethke; first gen. cassettes>Nakamichi CD1, azimuth adjusted>Korg MR1000 (1 bit 5.6MHz); 24/96 with Korg Audiogate; 16/44.1 by Izotope Ozone's MBIT+ (for all dithering), and Weiss Saracon SRC (all sample rate conversions). Transfer by Dave Cohen February 2011

ai_review.summary: Clear, slightly hissing audience tape captures a stellar 1983 summer show highlighted by a soaring Space > Other One and fiery Scarlet Fire.
ai_review.review: The recording, while bearing the expected tape hiss of a Bethke audience source, presents each instrument with surprising clarity. Musically the concert shines with standout performances of Birdsong, Sugaree, Scarlet Fire, an 18‑minute Space > The Other One jam, and high‑energy Wheel > Good Lovin' and US Blues, making it one of the era’s best shows.

ai_rating.rationale: All five reviews are strongly positive, praising both the performance (notably the Space > Other One and Scarlet Fire) and the surprisingly clear tape recording despite minor hiss.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally clear instrument separation with a bit of tape hiss; captures the band well for an audience recording and is considered an upgrade over other circulating sources.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set delivers strong moments with Birdsong and Sugaree, while the second set builds momentum through a hot Scarlet Fire and maintains energy into an epic Space > The Other One, then wraps up with high‑octane Wheel > Good Lovin' and a spirited US Blues.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia's vocal strength is highlighted and his guitar tone noted as solid.
band_member_comments.Phil: A hearty Phil Lesh bass intro before The Other One is specifically praised.
